title: Passing a uniform torsion bound to an affine limit
statement:
Let $X=\varprojlim_i X_i$ be a filtered inverse limit of
quasi-compact
quasi-separated schemes with affine transition maps.
If $\operatorname{cd}_{\rm tor}(X_i)\leq c$ for every $i$,
then $\operatorname{cd}_{\rm tor}(X)\leq c$, with bounds as in
[def-sc-etale-torsion-cd].

proof.text: Mathlib compactSpace_of_isLimit and isAffineHom_π_app make X quasi-compact and its projection affine; quasiSeparatedSpace_of_quasiSeparated then makes X quasi-separated. For a sheaf G killed by a positive integer n, use the constructed pull-push diagram and its reconstruction colimit. This implements the original proof step 1 by adjunction and finite-data descent.

Additivity of p_i* shows n annihilates G_i=p_i*G, hence G_i is torsion. By cohomology continuity every class of H^q(X,p_i^*G_i) is the pullback of a class of H^q(D_j,p_ji^*G_i) for a later stage j→i. Inverse image preserves torsion. Compare Sheaf.H with derived etale cohomology; the uniform stagewise dimension bound makes that group a subsingleton, so the class is zero.

Filtered-colimit commutation for Sheaf.H applied to reconstruction makes H^q(X,G) a subsingleton for every G killed by n>0. Apply the existing bounded-exponent torsion vanishing reduction, whose factorial-torsion filtration implements original step 3, to obtain the same result for every torsion F. The natural isomorphism with derived etale cohomology gives exactly the unchanged dimension bound.
